サイドボードのキャセロール皿を食卓中央の鍋敷きへ運び、長い辺がテーブルの縁と平行になるように置いてください。

Cradle bay on the charging-station tray that stops the cylindrical speaker rolling.
1 m USB charging cable whose connector matches the speaker's port.
USB charging hub with its mains lead disconnected.
Adhesive cable clip on the desk edge between the hub and the bay.
Hook-and-loop tie for the coiled slack.
Desk surface where the speaker starts.
Placing the speaker and inserting the connector.
Routing the cable into the clip, coiling the slack, and closing the tie.
Checking connector orientation and full insertion.
Powered-device rule: the hub has no mains power, so no current flows during the trial.
Safety: the speaker's lithium battery is checked for swelling, and the speaker is off.
The connector type and port position are checked on the physical speaker before the trial.

steps.description: Locate the speaker, the bay, the cable end, the clip, and the tie.
Grasp the speaker around its body.
Lift it off the desk.
Turn it so the charging port faces the hub side.
Lay it in the cradle bay.
Release the speaker.
Grasp the cable's free connector.
Line the connector up with the port in the correct orientation.
Push the connector in until it seats.
Checkpoint: confirm no connector metal is visible at the port.
Press the cable into the desk-edge clip.
Coil the remaining slack into loops.
Wrap and close the tie around the coil.
Verify all four goals and that the hub end is still plugged in.

success_criteria: The speaker lies in the cradle bay and does not roll when the tray is tapped once by hand.
On a close-up photograph, no metal of the connector shell is visible outside the port.
The cable passes through the desk-edge clip.
The slack is coiled into loops no more than 12 cm across, held by the closed tie, and no cable lies across the desk work area in front of the station.
Preservation check: the hub end is still fully plugged in.
setup: Disconnect the hub from mains.
Switch the speaker off and put it on the desk 40 cm from the bay.
Plug the cable into the hub and drape it loosely across the desk.
Lay the open tie beside the bay.
reset: Unplug the speaker end, open the tie, pull the cable out of the clip, and redrape it.
quality_checks: Close-up photograph of the port.
Overhead photograph of the station and cable path.
failure_modes: Hub end pulled out while routing
Speaker rolls out of the bay
Tie closed around the clip instead of the coil

requirements.reason: Utility closet with a sorting table and a shelf.
Primary GSO scan; a physical bin of this model is the cables bin.
Second physical bin of the same Curver model, for tape.
Third physical bin of the same Curver model, for hardware.
Three USB cables, each pre-rolled and tied.
Existing GSO gaffer tape roll, one of the tape items.
Masking tape roll, the second tape item.
Existing YCB padlock, one of the hardware items, closed and without a key.
Sealed zip bag of 20 wood screws, the second hardware item.
Three pre-printed label cards reading CABLES, TAPE, and HARDWARE.
Clip-on plastic label holders fitted to the front rim of each bin.
Shelf with three marked zones, numbered 1 to 3 from left to right.
Table where the items and empty bins start.
Placing the items, sliding in label cards, and carrying bins by their end handles.
Identifying item categories and reading labels.
The clip-on holders are fitted to each bin rim before the trial, so labelling means only inserting the card.
Safety: each filled bin is weighed and is within the setup's lift limit.
Safety: the shelf is no higher than 1.2 m so bins are not lifted overhead.
Safety: the screws stay sealed in their bag so no sharp loose parts are handled.

steps.description: Locate the items, the three empty bins, the label cards, and the shelf zones.
Identify each item's category.
Assign cables to the Curver bin, tape to the second bin, and hardware to the third.
Grasp each item in turn.
Place it in its category bin.
Release it.
Checkpoint: the table is clear and each bin holds only its category.
Grasp the label card that matches the first bin.
Line the card up with the bin's label holder.
Slide the card fully into the holder.
Release it and repeat for the other two bins.
Checkpoint: each label matches its bin's contents.
Grasp the cables bin by its end handles.
Lift it level.
Carry it to shelf zone 1.
Turn it so the label faces out.
Set it in the zone and release; repeat for tape in zone 2 and hardware in zone 3.
Verify the contents, labels, shelf order, and label direction.
Locate the bins, label cards, items, and shelf.
Slide the CABLES, TAPE, and HARDWARE cards into the three bins' holders.
Checkpoint: three distinct labels in place.
Sort each item into the bin whose label matches it.
Checkpoint: the table is clear and every item is in its labelled bin.
Carry each bin to its shelf zone, label out.
Verify the final state.

success_criteria: The Curver bin holds exactly the three rolled cables; the TAPE bin holds the gaffer and masking tape rolls; the HARDWARE bin holds the padlock and the bag of screws; no item is left on the table.
Each bin's label card reads its category, sits fully in its holder with no more than 5 mm protruding, and matches the bin's contents.
From left to right, the shelf holds CABLES in zone 1, TAPE in zone 2, and HARDWARE in zone 3, each bin's footprint fully inside its zone.
On a front photograph taken from 1 m, all three labels face out and are readable, and each bin's front edge is within 20 mm of the shelf lip.
setup: Fit a clip-on label holder to the front rim of each bin.
Scatter the five item groups on the table and set the three empty bins beside them.
Lay the three label cards face-up in random order.
Mark and number the three shelf zones.
reset: Take the bins down, remove the label cards, and scatter the items again.
quality_checks: Overhead photograph of each bin's contents at the stage 1 checkpoint.
Close-up photograph of each label.
Front photograph of the shelf from 1 m.
failure_modes: Tape roll put in the hardware bin
Label that does not match the contents
Bins shelved in the wrong order

Self-adhesive dummy shipping label, 100 x 150 mm.
Tray at the desk corner for items waiting for pickup.
Packing mat on the desk where the box is filled.
Desk surface where the drive starts.
Placing the drive and carrying the box.

Folding the box flaps closed.
Checking clearance, the tilt test, the seal, and label placement.
Powered-device rule: the drive is disconnected and no cable is attached during packing.

procedures.label: Pack at the mat, then set out

steps.description: Locate the drive, bag, box, void fill, slip, tape, label, and outgoing tray.
Grasp the drive by its long edges.
Slide it into the anti-static bag.
Press the bag's seal shut.
Lay the bagged drive flat and centred on the box's foam pad.
Pack crumpled void fill around all four sides and over the top.
Checkpoint: tilt the open box 30 degrees each way and confirm the drive moves no more than 5 mm and stays at least 30 mm from every wall.
Lay the packing slip on top of the fill.
Fold the inner flaps, then the outer flaps, closed.
Run tape along the centre seam, extending at least 50 mm down each end.
Checkpoint: the seam is fully covered and the flaps do not lift.
Line up the label on the top face, away from the seam.
Press the label flat from the centre outward.
Lift the box level.
Carry it to the outgoing-mail tray.
Set it label-up in the tray.
Release the box.
Verify the seal, the label, and the box in the tray.

success_criteria: Checkpoint before closing: the drive is inside the sealed anti-static bag, and with the box open and tilted 30 degrees each way it moves no more than 5 mm and stays at least 30 mm from every wall (photographed with a ruler).
Checkpoint before closing: the packing slip lies on top of the void fill.
Both outer flaps are closed and the centre seam is taped along its full length, with the tape running at least 50 mm down each end; no flap lifts when pressed lightly.
The label lies flat on the top face, fully on one flap and not across the seam, with no wrinkle or bubble wider than 10 mm.
The box sits label-up in the outgoing-mail tray.
setup: Pre-fold and tape the box bottom and lay the foam pad in the base.
Put the unplugged drive on the desk and the empty open box on the packing mat.
Lay out the bag, void fill, slip, tape dispenser, and label.
reset: Cut the tape with guarded scissors, unpack the drive, and replace the tape, label, and any torn void fill.
quality_checks: Top photograph with a ruler during the tilt checkpoint.
Photographs of the taped seam and each end.
Top photograph of the label.
failure_modes: Drive placed touching a box wall
Drive shifts on the tilt test
Label placed over the seam or wrinkled

draft_notes: gso_round3: 24 tasks on 24 further GSO models (9 atomic, 10 compound, 5 workflow).

gso_round3 part A: eight kitchen, dining, and pantry tasks on eight new Google Scanned Objects models (bundt pan, oblong casserole dish, fruit snack carton, herring tin, parchment sheet box, gold sprinkles bottle, chocolate cupcake carton, bead cereal bowl).

Granularity: three atomic (bundt pan inverted to drain, casserole dish on trivet, fruit snack carton stood in bin), four compound (pantry rotation by date, lining a pan with parchment, sprinkles closed and slotted, lunch packing in one packing zone with one carry to the shelf), one workflow (drying-rack unloading to three stores with dryness checkpoints).

New goals for the atlas: first-in-first-out rotation by date, lining a pan, labelled-slot baking-caddy organisation, lunch packing, and drying-rack unloading. Hang, stack-with-protector, and plain shelving patterns from gso_round1/2 are avoided.

Cross-links (referenced, not redefined): ycb_007_tuna_fish_can is the older stock in the rotation task; gso_object_lunch_box_dot (gso_round2) is lunch box A; gso_object_square_dinner_plate (gso_round2) is unloaded from the drying rack.

Thumbnails checked on Gazebo Fuel: the casserole dish is scanned without a lid (task uses it uncovered); the fruit snacks model is a closed carton whose front reads Fruit Medley despite the Grape model name; the herring, parchment, and cupcake models are retail packages and are named as such. Orbit_Bubblemint_Mini_Bottle_6_ct was dropped because its scan is a six-bottle retail carton, not the hanging mini bottle the candidate idea needed.
Templates: eight new template_gso_r3a_* templates, each listing its task's scene. No new concept or scene: objects use object_cookware, object_food_container, object_paper_item, and object_dish.

Resource IDs beginning gso_resource_ are planning object requirements (racks, stacks, bins, stickers, surrogates), not cataloged ObjectInstances; gso_resource_trivet, gso_resource_pantry_staging_surface, gso_resource_counter_packing_zone, and gso_resource_drying_towel reuse names from earlier GSO rounds.

Wet tasks (bundt pan, drying rack) declare robot_electronics_splash_protected. Food is sealed, surrogate, or not eaten; the casserole is served at room temperature. Every GSO scan is a single rigid mesh; flaps, caps, sheets, packs, water, and contents are real-object behaviour, so every asset_compatibility claim stays unknown.

gso_round3 part B (8 tasks): pink bath towel, olive washcloth, Reebok jogger, scrap collector, hair straightener, waffle dish towel, Teva bootie, hair-colour kit box. Groups: cleaning_laundry, bathroom_personal_care, footwear_clothing.

Granularity: 3 atomic (dish towel fold to template, bootie handover, hair-colour box above child reach), 3 compound (jogger pairing into a shoe bag, scrap collector hook-and-sweep, straightener clip-and-drawer), 2 workflow (laundry sort by colour then load, toiletry kit restock against a checklist).
New scene scene_home_laundry_area (laundry sort and dish-towel fold). Other tasks use scene_home_bathroom, scene_home_entryway, scene_home_bedroom, and scene_kitchen_counter.

Cross-links: ycb_074_t_shirt is sorted in the laundry workflow (its class is recorded at setup because its record gives no colour); gso_object_waste_basket (gso_round1) is the toiletry-kit discard bin; gso_object_tennis_shoe (gso_round1) is the decoy the jogger pairing must reject. None is redefined here.

Thumbnail checks (2026-09-25): all eight anchors are loose products except the hair-colour kit, which is the closed retail box and is named as such. The scrap collector scan has no lid, so the candidate's lid goal was dropped; the bootie shows no pull tab, so it is gripped at the collar. Two candidates were skipped for identity mismatches: Philips_Sonicare_Tooth_Brush_2_count shows an electric-toothbrush retail box, not a head pack, and Neat_Solutions_Character_Bib_2_pack shows a white square bowl, not a bib.
Eight new templates (template_gso_r3b_*). Existing handover templates are not reused because none lists scene_home_entryway and they live in other seeds.
Concepts: all objects reuse existing Atlas concepts (object_textile, object_footwear, object_receptacle, object_electronic_device, object_personal_care_container). No new concept.

Safety: the washer is unplugged or isolated and no cycle is started; the straightener is never powered and its plates must read 35 C or less; travel bottles hold water only; the hair-colour box is sealed or an empty carton; the handover limits approach speed and releases only on a confirmed grip; peelings are dry foam surrogates. No task uses water, so none declares robot_electronics_splash_protected.

All GSO scans are single rigid meshes; folding, rolling, drawstrings, zips, clips, cords, and handover grip are real-object behaviour, so every asset_compatibility claim stays unknown.
